entry.title: How do microSD Cards Store 2 TB in such a TINY space?

media:group.media:title: How do microSD Cards Store 2 TB in such a TINY space?
media:group.media:description:
Want cutting-edge tech articles? Get 20% off your subscription to IEEE Spectrum, the world's leading engineering magazine: https://spectrum.ieee.org/brancheducation
microSD Cards are the most compact and dense data storage format you can buy. Latest microSD Cards can store 2TB in a volume smaller than a penny! A shoebox full of them could hold every movie and TV show on your favorite streaming platform, with room to spare, and a room of microSD Cards can store the entirety of the internet. In this video, we open one up and journey down to the nanoscopic scale to see how 16 dies, each as thin as a strand of hair, filled with over 200 layers of NAND flash cells, store all your photos and files.

entry.title: How GPUs Are Printed With Light

media:group.media:title: How GPUs Are Printed With Light
media:group.media:description:
Inside this Nvidia graphics card is a GPU made from billions of transistors.
But before it becomes a chip, its microscopic design is printed onto a 300mm silicon wafer using an EUV photolithography system — a machine that can cost over $200 million.
Using extreme ultraviolet light, the machine prints one layer of each GPU chip at a time. In just seconds, it can pattern dozens of chips across a wafer, helping produce hundreds of thousands of microchips per day.
This is how modern GPUs are made.
Watch the full video on EUV Photolithography: https://youtu.be/B2482h_TNwg

entry.title: The Forgotten Apple Product that Revolutionized Computing #apple #computer

media:group.media:title: The Forgotten Apple Product that Revolutionized Computing #apple #computer
media:group.media:description:
The Apple II was Apple’s first commercially successful computer, released in 1977 and selling nearly 6 million units. Starting with just 4KB of RAM and powered by the MOS 6502 CPU, this early personal computer could run applications and classic games like The Oregon Trail. In this teardown, we explore the Apple II’s internal hardware, including ROM, DRAM, and expansion slots, and break down how this revolutionary system helped shape modern computing. From its $7,000 starting price to its simple yet powerful architecture, the Apple II is a key piece of tech history.
Watch the full breakdown: https://youtu.be/16zrEPOsIcI

media:group.media:title: Zooming Into a CPU (It's Incredible)
media:group.media:description:
When you zoom into a CPU, SoC, or any microchip in general, you'll find a nanoscopic sea of transistors, each just a few nanometers wide, grouped into logic gates called standard cells. To wire a full processor together, it takes 18 stacked layers upon layers of intricate wiring with the transistors at the bottom and then progressively larger wires up top — all connected vertically by vias.
Watch the full video to see how it all fits together. 🔬https://youtu.be/_Pqfjer8-O4

entry.title: The Most Expensive Machine Ever Made

media:group.media:title: The Most Expensive Machine Ever Made
media:group.media:description:
A massive excavator can cost $25 million. A Falcon 9 rocket costs around $67 million. An F-35 fighter jet can cost around $100 million.
But a single EUV photolithography system can cost over $200 million — and it’s used to print the microscopic patterns inside modern microchips.
Even crazier? Advanced chip factories can have dozens of these machines, making the entire facility cost close to $20 billion.
This is why modern chip manufacturing is one of the most expensive industries on Earth.

entry.title: How does Computer Cache, Memory, and Storage Work? 🖥️💿🛠️

media:group.media:title: How does Computer Cache, Memory, and Storage Work? 🖥️💿🛠️
media:group.media:description:
To learn more about how Micron memory and storage help enable AI at every level, visit: https://tinyurl.com/Micron-AI-data-center
Interested in working with Micron to make cutting-edge memory and storage solutions? Work at Micron: https://tinyurl.com/Micron-Careers
Your computer has over a dozen different memory and storage locations—from CPU registers to DRAM, SSDs and hard drives—and it needs every single one. In this video, you’ll see exactly why. We're breaking down the entire explanation of the memory hierarchy into three parts. First, a visual analogy using books and libraries that finally makes the wild tradeoffs in speed, capacity, and cost click. Second, a nanoscopic tour inside registers, SRAM cache, DRAM, 3D NAND SSDs, and spinning hard drives to see how each one physically stores bits. Third, the insane memory and storage stack powering modern AI servers, from HBM3E stacks to petabyte-scale NVMe data lakes. By the end, you'll understand exactly how your computer—and the AI servers training the world's largest models—juggle data across every layer of the hierarchy.
Notes about the content: As our example computer, we’re using a typical computer from 2026. Of course, the specs vary based on the devices and the age of your computer, but all are within the ballpark. Also, we chose to keep the units consistent when comparing the devices, which is why we focus on nanosecond access time rather than the number of clock cycles. Consistency between units, we felt, was more important to get a sense of the magnitudes of difference.

You’ve probably heard that computers operate using logic gates — but have you ever wondered how they actually work? Logic gates are the fundamental building blocks of all digital systems, from tiny microcontrollers to powerful CPUs. In this short, we focus on one of the simplest yet most important ones: the AND gate.
We’ll take a close-up look at its internal circuitry, show how transistors are arranged to implement logical operations, and explain what happens at the electrical level when inputs change. entry.title: How does a Laser Computer Mouse Work? #mouse #howitworks #laser

media:group.media:title: How does a Laser Computer Mouse Work? #mouse #howitworks #laser
media:group.media:description:
Ever wondered how a computer mouse actually works? 🖱️ Using clean and easy-to-follow 3D animation, this short takes you inside one of the most important tools we use every day. Beneath its simple design is smart technology working constantly in real time.
An optical sensor on the bottom of the mouse scans the surface thousands of times per second. A tiny processor compares these images to detect direction and speed, turning your hand movements into smooth cursor motion on screen. Each click activates precise switches that instantly send signals to your computer, while the scroll wheel uses a rotating encoder to control scrolling with accuracy.
Whether wired or wireless, the mouse communicates with your computer in milliseconds, making everything feel fast and effortless. From browsing and gaming to design and animation, this small device plays a big role in how we interact with digital worlds.

entry.title: The Engineering that Runs the Digital World 🛠️⚙️💻 How do CPUs Work?

media:group.media:title: The Engineering that Runs the Digital World 🛠️⚙️💻 How do CPUs Work?
media:group.media:description:
Go to http://brilliant.org/BranchEducation/ for a 30-day free trial and expand your knowledge. Use this link to get a 20% discount on their annual premium membership.
Have you ever wondered how CPUs work? Well, in this video, we take a 3D animated tour of a Central Processing Unit and see exactly how it works. Central Processing Units, or CPUs, are incredibly complicated, and they practically run the modern world. CPUs can be found in every desktop computer, laptop, video game console, smartphone, and any other device you use on a daily basis. CPUs are built from tens of billions of transistors assembled into billions of logic gates, and essentially they're amazingly powerful calculators. But in reality, they're more like instruction-crunching and data-moving machines. All CPUs share a common DNA, which is the Fetch-Decode-Execute cycle. This cycle is both very powerful and a critical limitation of every CPU. So dive right in and we'll show you how CPUs work.
